search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 1017 - PDF page 497 (word id 77425) (w2/2)
search_lead.cognate: Armenian չտեսին is negative aorist plural of tesanem, cognate with Greek δρακέντες/δεδορκότας through derḱ-. Armenian զլոյս is accusative of loys (leuk-); Greek φάος replaces the light noun with phāos (bʰeh₂-).
search_lead.argument: Death includes even those who have not seen the light of the world; Pindar speaks of birth under Eileithyia, and Euripides contrasts death with seeing light. Same transitive see-light life metaphor with noun renewal. Only an external lead: Christian/biblical transmission must be excluded before inheritance can be argued.

search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 1003 - PDF page 483 (word id 71266)
search_lead.cognate: Armenian սիրտ and Greek κραδίη continue the heart root ḱerd-. Stone/metal predicates are semantically comparable but no cognacy is claimed for their material words.
search_lead.argument: Armenian asks who could have a stone heart or bronze body and refrain from tears at Christ’s suffering; Telemachus calls Penelope’s heart harder than stone, while Iliad 4 denies bodies are stone or iron. A potentially traditional hardness metaphor, but the Armenian’s stone-heart/bronze-flesh combination also recalls biblical Job 6:12 and cannot be assigned to PIE from these witnesses.

search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 958 - PDF page 438 (word id 51950) (w1/2)
search_lead.cognate: Armenian գործովք (gorc, instrumental plural) and Greek ἔργῳ/ἔργων continue wérǵom. Armenian բանիւք (ban, instrumental plural, mislemmatized in slab) replaces Greek epos with a bʰeh₂- speech noun.
search_lead.argument: Instrumental words-and-deeds merism in Armenian moral exhortation compares with Greek instrumental word-or-deed and anger at words and deeds; BS-1e00a also contrasts the two. Formal comparison is stronger than the assigned partners, but scriptural and Christian ethical usage provides a plausible transmission route. Recorded for separate review, not claimed inherited.

search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 1018 - PDF page 498 (word id 78263) (w1/4)
search_lead.cognate: Armenian քուն and Greek ὕπνος continue swopno-/supno-; Armenian յաչաց (ablative plural of akn) and Greek ὄμμασι share the eye root h₃ekʷ-.
search_lead.argument: Armenian sleep is cut off from mourners’ eyes; Agamemnon lacks sleep upon his eyes, and Athena pours sleep on Odysseus’s eyes. A cognate sleep-eye association with different relational syntax and verbs. The vigil context makes the comparison worth review, but natural bodily association and biblical mediation limit its evidential value.
